body_long:
Four Seasons has named 13 hotels and resorts it expects to open in 2027 and beyond, in a release published on 20 October 2026. The list mixes returning icons, conversions of historic buildings and new destinations for the brand.

## Europe

The Park Gstaad returns after a transformation led by designer Joseph Dirand, more than a century after the hotel first opened in 1910. In Berlin, Four Seasons Hotel Berlin will occupy the former Hotel de Rome, a 19th-century building that was once the headquarters of Dresdner Bank.

## Asia

Four Seasons Resort and Residences Okinawa will be the brand's first resort in Japan, set on 100 acres of coastline and designed by Kengo Kuma with Kuniken.

## Middle East and Africa

The Middle East is the largest cluster on the list. Four Seasons Hotel Madinah will stand steps from the Prophet's Mosque, while Four Seasons Hotel and Residences Jeddah at the Corniche will face the Red Sea near Al-Balad. In Egypt, the brand plans Four Seasons Hotel Luxor, a gateway to the city's temples and tombs, and a hotel with private residences in Madinaty, Cairo. Four Seasons Hotel Beirut adds 230 rooms and suites with a rooftop pool, and Four Seasons Resort Zanzibar spans 126 acres of beachfront, complementing the brand's safari property in Tanzania.

## The Americas

The list also includes Four Seasons Resort The Biltmore Santa Barbara, a beachfront retreat returning to the brand; a resort at Tropicalia on Samaná Bay in the Dominican Republic, designed by Isay Weinfeld; a private island resort on Caye Chapel in Belize, with a golf course by Greg Norman and a conservation institute led by Fabien Cousteau; and a hotel anchoring the redeveloped Shipyards waterfront in Jacksonville.

## The signal

Several entries are reopenings or conversions of historic hotels rather than new builds: Gstaad, Berlin and Santa Barbara among them. For owners of heritage assets in Europe, a global brand is increasingly a partner for the next chapter, not only for ground-up projects. The Swiss and German entries also bring Four Seasons closer to the European clientele that already fills its French addresses.

Congratulations to the Four Seasons development and opening teams.
